title: Type 2 diabetes: targets and the 2026 medicines pathway
blurb: Apply the NICE NG28 (2026) HbA1c targets and the new first-line medicines: metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor, adding semaglutide in cardiovascular disease.
question: Mr Mensah, 61, has just been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He had a myocardial infarction 2 years ago and has no kidney disease. Which medicines does NICE recommend he is offered first?

teach.body: Type 2 diabetes is driven by insulin resistance and declining insulin secretion. NICE NG28 was substantially updated in February 2026. The old sequence (metformin first, then add another drug later) has been replaced: most adults are now offered modified-release metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor together from the start, chosen around their heart, kidney and frailty status. Plain English: treat the person's whole cardiovascular and renal risk, not just the glucose number.

head: Situation
Aim for
rows: Diet, or medicine not causing hypos
On a medicine associated with hypos
Older or frail, high hypo risk
teach.caption: Measure HbA1c every 3–6 months until stable on unchanging therapy, then every 6 months (1.5.1).

children.label: MR metformin
children.sub: SGLT-2i if frailty does not add risk

teach.caption: If metformin is contraindicated or not tolerated, the SGLT-2 inhibitor (with semaglutide in CVD) is offered without it. In frailty, choose an SGLT-2 inhibitor or a DPP-4 inhibitor by frailty risk (1.19.2).

teach.body: Before starting medicines, assess cardiovascular and renal status, and frailty if it is a concern. With eGFR 30 or more: MR metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor. eGFR 20 to below 30: dapagliflozin or empagliflozin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor. eGFR below 20: consider a DPP-4 inhibitor, then pioglitazone or insulin-based treatment if needed.

teach.caption: If HbA1c falls below target without hypos, encourage maintaining it, but consider causes such as declining kidney function or sudden weight loss (1.5.10).

teach.text: Do not teach the old 'metformin alone first' sequence. Under NG28 (2026), adults with no relevant comorbidity are offered modified-release metformin AND an SGLT-2 inhibitor together. Also, 58 mmol/mol is the trigger to intensify, not a target: the aim then becomes 53.

items.label: may need to delay or pause treatment

teach.caption: NICE NG28 recs 1.21.1–1.21.3. DKA on these drugs can occur with near-normal glucose.

teach.h: Scenario: Mrs Hughes, 84, in the GP practice
teach.body: Mrs Hughes has type 2 diabetes, lives alone, falls often and has postural dizziness. Her HbA1c is 60 mmol/mol on gliclazide. The practice nurse recognises falls risk and hypoglycaemia risk, so the team discusses relaxing her target and reviewing the sulfonylurea. With frailty, NICE offers MR metformin, and an SGLT-2 inhibitor only if her frailty does not put her at risk of volume depletion or hypotension.

teach.h: What the nurse checks and teaches
items: Agree an individual HbA1c target and recheck every 3–6 months until stable.
Sick-day rules in every plan: which medicines (metformin, SGLT-2 inhibitors) to pause if dehydrated, vomiting or with diarrhoea, and how to restart.
Ask about low-carbohydrate or ketogenic diets before and during SGLT-2 inhibitor use.
Use the smallest effective number of medicines at the lowest effective dose in frailty.
HbA1c aims: 48 (no hypo-causing drug), 53 (hypo-causing drug); intensify at 58, aiming for 53.
First line 2026: MR metformin + SGLT-2 inhibitor; add SC semaglutide in atherosclerotic CVD.
eGFR 20–29: dapagliflozin or empagliflozin + DPP-4 inhibitor; below 20: DPP-4 inhibitor.
Frailty: metformin; SGLT-2i only if frailty does not add volume or hypotension risk.
Check DKA risk before SGLT-2 inhibitors; sick-day rules cover restarting too.

summary: You can now set the NG28 HbA1c target from the person's medicines and frailty, and recognise when to intensify. You can also explain the 2026 first-line pathway of metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor, with semaglutide in cardiovascular disease and adjustments for kidney function and frailty.

A.q: Mr Lim, 55, manages his type 2 diabetes with diet and modified-release metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor. What HbA1c should he be supported to aim for?
A.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.5.7: on diet or medicines not associated with hypoglycaemia, aim for HbA1c 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).

whyNot.1: 53 mmol/mol is the aim for people on a medicine associated with hypoglycaemia.
whyNot.2: 58 mmol/mol is the level at which medicines are intensified, not a target.
whyNot.3: 42 mmol/mol is not a NICE target and would increase hypoglycaemia risk for some.

A.q: Mrs Ali, 49, has newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, no heart failure, no cardiovascular disease and normal kidney function. Which initial treatment does NICE NG28 (2026) recommend?
options: A sulfonylurea plus a DPP-4 inhibitor
Modified-release metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor
A.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.13.1 (2026): for adults with no relevant comorbidity, offer modified-release metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor.

whyNot.0: Starting metformin and reviewing later is the pre-2026 sequence, replaced by metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor from the start.
whyNot.1: Neither drug is the NG28 first-line choice for someone without comorbidity.
whyNot.2: Insulin is not first line here; it is reserved for symptomatic hyperglycaemia or later steps.

A.q: Mr Mensah, 61, has type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease after a previous myocardial infarction. Which combination should he be offered?
options: MR metformin, an SGLT-2i and SC semaglutide
A.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.15.1: with atherosclerotic CVD, offer MR metformin, an SGLT-2 inhibitor and subcutaneous semaglutide (up to 1 mg weekly) for cardiovascular, renal and glycaemic benefit.

whyNot.0: DPP-4 inhibitors are used in severe CKD or frailty, not for CVD benefit.
whyNot.2: Pioglitazone is a later option in very low eGFR, not the CVD pathway.
whyNot.3: Sulfonylureas carry hypoglycaemia risk and are not in the CVD first-line combination.

B.q: Mrs Okoro's HbA1c has risen to 59 mmol/mol on her initial regimen. What does NICE advise?
options: Keep current treatment and recheck in 12 months
Reinforce advice, aim for 53 and intensify
B.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.5.8: if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol or higher, reinforce diet, healthy living and adherence advice, support an aim of 53 mmol/mol, and intensify medicines.

whyNot.0: Waiting 12 months ignores the 58 mmol/mol trigger to act.
whyNot.1: Relaxing targets is for selected older or frailer people, not a default response to a rise.
whyNot.3: Intensifying does not mean abandoning metformin or jumping straight to insulin.

B.q: Mr Brown has type 2 diabetes and an eGFR of 24 mL/min/1.73 m². Which treatment does NICE NG28 recommend?
options: Dapagliflozin or empagliflozin plus a DPP-4i
MR metformin and any SGLT-2 inhibitor
B.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.18.2: with eGFR 20 to below 30, offer dapagliflozin or empagliflozin and a DPP-4 inhibitor.

whyNot.1: Metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor is the plan when eGFR is 30 or more.
whyNot.2: Pioglitazone is considered when eGFR is below 20 and a DPP-4 inhibitor is unsuitable.
whyNot.3: Semaglutide is added for atherosclerotic CVD; it is not the NG28 plan for eGFR 20 to below 30.

B.q: Before starting an SGLT-2 inhibitor, which finding should prompt the nurse to flag a raised risk of diabetic ketoacidosis?
options: A family history of type 2 diabetes
B.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.21.1: check DKA risk before starting an SGLT-2 inhibitor, for example a previous DKA, intercurrent illness, dehydration risk or a very low-carbohydrate or ketogenic diet.

whyNot.0: Obesity is not listed as a DKA risk; NG28 offers metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor in obesity.
whyNot.2: Family history of type 2 diabetes does not raise DKA risk.
whyNot.3: A raised HbA1c is a reason to treat, not a listed DKA risk factor.

C.q: Mrs Hughes, 84, has type 2 diabetes, recurrent falls and postural hypotension. Her HbA1c is 60 mmol/mol on gliclazide and she lives alone. Which approach best reflects NICE NG28?
options: Add insulin to bring HbA1c below 53
Add an SGLT-2 inhibitor to her gliclazide
Consider relaxing her target and review gliclazide
C.why: NICE NG28 recs 1.5.9 and 1.19.1–1.19.3: consider relaxing the HbA1c target for older or frailer people at high risk from hypoglycaemia (such as falls), and review treatment to the smallest effective number of medicines. SGLT-2 inhibitors are offered in frailty only where volume depletion or hypotension is not a risk.

whyNot.0: Tight control increases hypoglycaemia and falls risk in frailty.
whyNot.1: Insulin adds hypoglycaemia risk and burden for a frail person living alone.
whyNot.2: Her postural hypotension means an SGLT-2 inhibitor could cause harm through volume depletion.

C.q: Mr Sato, 35, has just been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He has no other conditions. Which plan matches NICE NG28 for early onset type 2 diabetes?
options: MR metformin, SGLT-2i, consider GLP-1 RA
A sulfonylurea plus a DPP-4 inhibitor
C.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.16.1: early onset (diagnosed before 40), offer MR metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor and consider adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist (or tirzepatide for glycaemic benefit).

whyNot.0: Metformin then review is the replaced pre-2026 sequence; early onset needs combination treatment.
whyNot.2: Delaying medicines in early onset disease is not NG28 advice.
whyNot.3: Neither drug is the NG28 early onset pathway.

C.q: Mrs Rossi, 66, takes MR metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor. Her HbA1c has fallen to 44 mmol/mol over 6 months and she has lost 8 kg without trying. What should the nurse do?
options: Congratulate her and keep the plan unchanged
Encourage her to aim lower, near 40
Report the weight loss for further assessment
Stop metformin so HbA1c rises back to 48
C.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.5.10: if HbA1c falls below target without hypoglycaemia, encourage maintaining it, but be aware of other reasons for a low HbA1c such as deteriorating renal function or sudden weight loss. Unintentional weight loss needs assessment.

whyNot.0: Unexplained weight loss is a warning sign NICE asks you to consider.
whyNot.1: Pushing lower is not advised and ignores the possible cause.
whyNot.3: Stopping medicines to raise HbA1c is not appropriate; the cause needs finding.

reteach.title: Protect the heart and kidneys first
reteach.question: Imagine NG28 (2026) as a builder who asks 'what is this house built on?' before choosing materials. What does the nurse check first?

blocks.body: First check the foundations: heart (heart failure, atherosclerotic disease), kidneys (eGFR) and frailty. Then the materials: most people get MR metformin plus an SGLT-2 inhibitor; atherosclerotic disease adds semaglutide; low eGFR swaps to specific SGLT-2 inhibitors with a DPP-4 inhibitor; frailty may mean metformin without the SGLT-2 inhibitor. Targets follow the medicine: 48 if no hypo risk, 53 if there is.

blocks.text: 58 is the trigger, 53 is the aim. A rise to 58 or higher means intensify and aim for 53.

explain.body: Aim for 48 mmol/mol on diet or drugs not linked to hypos; 53 on drugs linked to hypos. If HbA1c reaches 58 or more, reinforce advice, aim for 53 and intensify.

test.q: Mr Davies takes gliclazide for type 2 diabetes. What HbA1c should he aim for?
test.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.5.7: on a medicine associated with hypoglycaemia (such as a sulfonylurea), aim for 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).

whyNot.0: 48 applies when the medicine does not cause hypoglycaemia.

explain.body: No relevant comorbidity, heart failure or obesity: MR metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor. If metformin is not tolerated, SGLT-2 inhibitor monotherapy.

test.q: A woman with type 2 diabetes and heart failure cannot tolerate metformin. What does NICE offer?
options: A DPP-4 inhibitor such as sitagliptin
test.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.14.2: if metformin is contraindicated or not tolerated in heart failure, offer SGLT-2 inhibitor monotherapy.

whyNot.0: Sulfonylureas are not the NG28 heart failure alternative.
whyNot.1: DPP-4 inhibitors appear in the low eGFR and frailty pathways.
whyNot.3: Pioglitazone causes fluid retention and is not offered here.

explain.body: Atherosclerotic CVD: add subcutaneous semaglutide (Ozempic), up to 1 mg once a week, to MR metformin and an SGLT-2 inhibitor, for cardiovascular, renal and glycaemic benefits.

test.q: How is the semaglutide recommended for type 2 diabetes with atherosclerotic CVD given?
test.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.15.1: subcutaneous semaglutide up to 1 mg once a week.

whyNot.0: NG28 specifies the subcutaneous weekly form here.

explain.body: eGFR 30+: metformin + SGLT-2i. eGFR 20–29: dapagliflozin or empagliflozin + DPP-4i. Below 20: DPP-4i. Frailty: metformin, with an SGLT-2i only if frailty does not raise the risk of volume depletion or hypotension.

test.q: Mr Evans has type 2 diabetes and an eGFR of 16 mL/min/1.73 m². What does NICE suggest considering first?
test.why: NICE NG28 rec 1.18.3: with eGFR below 20, consider a DPP-4 inhibitor.

whyNot.1: Metformin is used with eGFR 30 or more.
whyNot.2: This combination is for eGFR 30 or more.
whyNot.3: A ketogenic diet is not a treatment step and raises DKA risk with SGLT-2 inhibitors.
